title: An abelian scheme over a Dedekind base has the Néron mapping property
statement: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $E$ and let $T$ be a nonempty open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $B\to T$ be a smooth proper commutative group scheme with connected fibres [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every smooth $T$-scheme $X$, restriction to the generic fibre is a bijection $$\operatorname{Hom}_T(X,B)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,B_E),$$ where $X_E=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $B_E=B\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-pc-base-change]. There is no quasi-compactness assumption on $X$. Here a Dedekind domain means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A group scheme over a scheme $T$ consists of multiplication, inverse and identity $T$-morphisms satisfying the group diagrams; it is commutative if multiplication is invariant under interchange of the two factors. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: First prove uniqueness on any smooth $T$-scheme $Z$. In [lem-sbc-finite-etale-generic-fibre-cover-density], take $S=T$, $C=Z$ and the identity etale map $Z\to Z$. It gives that $Z$ is reduced and $Z_E\to Z$ has dense image. Properness of $B\to T$ includes separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext], with $h:Z_E\to Z$ and $s:B\to T$, shows that two $T$-morphisms $Z\to B$ agreeing on the generic fibre are equal. This applies to open overlaps as well as to $X$ itself.

source.place: 1.2 Proposition 8, final sentence; uniqueness written in relative dominant-map form

proof.text: Fix $f_E:X_E\to B_E$. Cover $X$ by affine open subschemes $U_i$ [def-pc-scheme]. Each $U_i\to T$ is smooth: the local finite-presentation charts and the local infinitesimal lifting property defining smoothness restrict to open subschemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-generic-map-big-open] to $U_i$, the proper target $B$, and $f_E|_{(U_i)_E}$. Obtain $V_i\subseteq U_i$ and $v_i:V_i\to B$, with $(V_i)_E=(U_i)_E$, $(v_i)_E=f_E|_{(U_i)_E}$, $V_i$ dense in each fibre, and $V_i$ containing every point with local-ring dimension at most one. These are precisely the domain hypotheses needed below.

source.place: 1.2 Proposition 8, first claim and its valuative/spreading argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-weil-codimension-extension] with source $U_i$, group scheme $G=B$, domain $V_i$ and morphism $v_i$. The base $T$ is exactly the specified open of the Dedekind spectrum; $B$ is smooth and separated, and the preceding step supplies fibrewise density and definition at every point of codimension at most one. We obtain $F_i:U_i\to B$ extending $v_i$. Since $(V_i)_E=(U_i)_E$, the equality $(F_i)_E=f_E|_{(U_i)_E}$ holds on the whole generic fibre, not just on a dense subopen.

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the restrictions of $F_i$ and $F_j$ have the same generic restriction, namely that of $f_E$. This overlap is an open subscheme of the smooth $X$ and hence smooth by the same local-definition argument as above. Step 1 therefore gives equality on the entire overlap. The morphisms glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to $F:X\to B$. Their composites with $B\to T$ equal the structure map on each $U_i$, so the glued morphism is over $T$. Its generic restriction is $f_E$ because this equality holds on every $(U_i)_E$. Step 1 gives uniqueness of $F$. The open cover may be infinite; no intersection was assumed affine. If $X$ is empty, the same gluing statement gives the unique empty-source map. Restriction is therefore both surjective and injective.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q68-2ec627161 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and the BLR route (1.2 Prop 8, 4.4 Thm 1, S-rational meaning dense in each fibre); BLR is not in the local literature and is WANTED. Item steps: (1) T is integral, so the generic-fibre-density lemma with the identity étale map gives a reduced source with dense generic fibre, and the separated-dominant leaf gives uniqueness. (2) Affine cover, then the proper-target big-open node on each U_i. (3) The relative Weil node, whose hypotheses are exactly fibrewise density and every point with dim O<=1, which step 2 supplies; (V_i)_E=(U_i)_E gives the generic equality. (4) Smooth overlaps plus step 1, then gluing over an arbitrary cover, with no affine intersections assumed. New node lem-sfb-proper-generic-map-big-open is true; I proved it independently (spread f_E over an open T', finitely many generic points of the closed fibres, DVR stalks by normality and the flat dimension formula, valuative criterion and gluing), and the example x/π on A^1 over a DVR is consistent with it. New node lem-sfb-relative-weil-codimension-extension is exactly BLR 4.4/1 over a Dedekind open; ū|_V=u holds by reducedness and separatedness; units on A^2 minus a point extend, and the group hypothesis is necessary. Neither node restates a clause of the item, and their composition is BLR's proof. Duplicate checks: the field-base Weil extension and divisorial-indeterminacy nodes, valuation-stalk, rational-map-extension-valuation-point, Nagata–Conrad blow-up, the semiabelian homomorphism-extension nodes and the Néron DVR criterion; none is a duplicate. No cycle. Accepted tool_uses: lem-sbc-finite-etale-generic-fibre-cover-density and the gluing leaf.
